chunks.arabic_text: يُونُسُ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Yūnus, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: «إِذَا قَتَلَ الْعَبْدُ الْحُرَّ دُفِعَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ، فَإِنْ شَاءُوا قَتَلُوهُ، وَإِنْ شَاءُوا حَبَسُوهُ يَكُونُ عَبْدًا لَهُمْ، وَإِنْ شَاءُوا اسْتَرَقُّوهُ».

translations.en: “When a slave kills a free man, he is handed over to the heirs of the slain person. If they wish, they may kill him; if they wish, they may detain him so that he becomes a slave belonging to them; and if they wish, they may enslave him.”

en.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning retaliation and the options available to the heirs of a free person killed by a slave. It outlines their authority over the offender, including execution, detention as their slave, or enslavement, within the framework of judicial rulings in cases of homicide.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave kills a free man in Shia fiqh?

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the slave; the offender in this legal case
key_terms.الْحُرَّ: the free person; the victim whose legal status affects the ruling
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person who hold the right of response
key_terms.قَتَلُوهُ: they may kill him; exercise retaliation
key_terms.حَبَسُوهُ: they may detain him and hold him under their possession
key_terms.عَبْدًا لَهُمْ: a slave belonging to them; under their ownership
key_terms.اسْتَرَقُّوهُ: they may enslave him; take him into slavery
